customer_question: Can the InterLab control PC also be used to run the DUT-mode-entry application and a status/LAN connection for the device under test, or will that interfere with RF PHY testing?
question_variants: Is it OK to install the chipset vendor's app on the InterLab control PC?
Why did our LAN setup with the InterLab control PC cause TCP-client problems on one model but not another?
What's the safe way to connect the DUT to the InterLab control PC without breaking the RF PHY bridge?
How do we troubleshoot a failed Bluetooth LE Direct Mode connection between the bridge-app PC and the DUT?
actual_issue: During RF PHY testing of two different models, the lab attempted to use the InterLab control PC to also run a DUT-mode-entry application and a LAN-connected status application, which worked for one model (DUT connected via Serial-over-USB) but caused TCP-client and connectivity problems on the other model, and it was unclear which applications can safely share the InterLab control PC during active testing versus which ones cannot.
plain_english_explanation: The PC that runs the certification lab's measurement equipment is busy talking to that equipment throughout the whole test, so anything else that needs a constant, real-time connection to the device under test can't share that same PC without risking interference. Apps that only need to run briefly before the actual measurement starts are fine to share. The team ran into trouble because they tried to make one PC do both jobs at once for one of the two test models, and had to work out which specific app was actually the problem.
consultant_answer: For the model where the DUT connects via Serial-over-USB, it is fine to also use the InterLab control PC to run the DUT-mode-entry application -- InterLab's own Automation Explore feature can even put the DUT into test mode directly, without needing the chipset vendor's app at all. For the other model, the team tried connecting the InterLab PC and DUT via a LAN cable to use the same shared-PC approach, but ran into problems: InterLab's measurement instrument cluster is controlled by the control PC via GPIB-over-Ethernet, and this model's RF PHY test setup requires the DUT to continuously exchange commands and data over LAN with 'the PC running the QUTS Status APP' throughout the test -- so the InterLab control PC must not be reused for that LAN role. The actual restriction is specifically on the RF PHY protocol-bridge application that runs during the live test, not on the DUT-mode-entry application, which only runs before testing starts and is therefore safe to coexist on the control PC. When the LAN-based status app failed to expose a 'Configure TCP Client' option needed to set up the connection, the consultant suspected the DUT-side TCP listener may have been altered by the earlier improper sharing attempt, and recommended reinstalling the status app (while noting this was unlikely to fix it if the affected PC hadn't otherwise been touched) and checking the cabling, Media Converter power, and bridge-app PC's IP address, then reissuing the relevant setup script and retrying the chipset vendor's Bluetooth LE Direct Mode connection procedure.
decision_logic: The deciding factor is not whether an application is from the chipset vendor or third party, but whether it needs to run continuously during the live RF PHY measurement: applications that run only before the test starts (e.g., DUT-mode entry) can safely share the InterLab control PC, while a protocol-bridge application that exchanges commands and data with the DUT throughout the measurement must run on a separate PC, since the control PC's GPIB-over-Ethernet duties to the instrument cluster cannot be interrupted or contended with.
final_recommendation: Keep any during-test RF PHY bridge/protocol-conversion application on a PC separate from the InterLab control PC; it is acceptable to run a pre-test DUT-mode-entry application on the control PC itself. If a LAN-based connection to the DUT fails to establish, check the physical cabling and Media Converter power first, confirm the bridge-app PC's IP address, reissue the relevant setup script, and retry the chipset vendor's documented connection procedure before escalating to the customer.
risk_if_done_wrong: Running a during-test RF PHY bridge application on the same PC as InterLab's instrument control caused TCP-client setup failures and lost troubleshooting time, and risked corrupting the DUT-side connection state in a way that required reinstalling software and re-verifying physical connections to recover.
